brief: The allotment block is a vegetable block that does not contain only vegetables. The opening scatter seeds ornamentals into the plots — seed 42 opens with a fern in the block, seed 7 with a fern and a lavender — because speciesFor() filters only NEW sowing, not the initial scatter. Since #29 that matters in a way it did not before: harvestPlot() pays its cells into produce[], stockMarket() lays them out, and the town can now put a fern on a market stall as something a gardener grew to sell. Make the block vegetables from the first frame. NOTE: issued at #36 and consumed by a harness fault before any worker ran — no prior attempt exists.
successLooksLike: Over ten seeds, no non-vegetable species ever occupies an allotment plot at t=0 or reaches mkShelf at any point in a folded year, and the courtyard beds are unchanged — the same eleven species in the same proportions as HEAD, proven against a stashed baseline.
avoid: Do not fix it by filtering at the market — that is a second predicate for what an allotment grows and it will drift from speciesFor(). Fix it where the block is populated. Expect the census to churn everywhere: any change to the opening scatter reshuffles the seeded world, so read the diff for collapse, not delta.
